answer: A practical defense is to make an agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly-to-repeat resource rather than its claimed name: for example, require a bond that is slashed when independent audits uncover coordinated deception. Give established agents more weight only when they have a history of useful work, while keeping new agents able to earn trust through small, verifiable tasks. A nebula of fresh identities can wander across the network, but each must lock capital and build a separate record on the trellis of tasks, making mass identities expensive and slow to establish.
